Introduction

Welcome back to Ovi English School.

Picture this.

You have six tabs open.

One is a hotel, one is a train ticket, and one is a review page.

Then you stop and think, which one was the best choice?

Microsoft says Edge can now help.

Its AI tool, Copilot, can look across your open tabs and answer questions about them.

That may sound helpful, but it also brings a clear question.

Would you let AI read your tabs to save time?

Today we will look at Microsoft’s update, what it can do, and why some people may feel excited while others feel careful.

Practice

What can Copilot now do with open tabs in Edge?

It can read information from several open tabs and answer questions about them.

In Sara’s example, what did she want Copilot to compare?

She wanted it to compare two hotels and tell her which was closer and cheaper.

What does the word “experimental” mean in this story?

It means the feature was still being tested and improved.

What is a simple meaning of “agentic features”?

It means the AI does not only answer questions.

It can also take actions for the user.

What is the main benefit and the main risk of this update?

The main benefit is saving time.

The main risk is losing control or sharing private information.

Summary

Today’s story is simple but important.

Microsoft Edge wants to do more than open websites.

With Copilot, it can now compare and summarize your open tabs.

That may help when you shop, travel, or read online.

But people will still ask careful questions about privacy, mistakes, and control.

So maybe the real answer is this: AI can be a helpful assistant, but users still need to stay awake and choose wisely.
